html:
Chilean poet and diplomat, one of the most widely read poets of the 20th century. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971.

Born Ricardo Neftalí Reyes in southern Chile, he took his pen name as a teenager. In his school town, Temuco, the poet Gabriela Mistral encouraged him. Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair (1924), written when he was nineteen, made him famous across the Spanish-speaking world.

As a consul he served in Asia and then Spain, where the Spanish Civil War and the murder of his friend Federico García Lorca turned him to politics. In 1939 he organised a ship that carried some 2,000 Spanish Republican refugees to Chile.

He joined the Communist Party and was elected senator. When the party was banned in 1948 he went into hiding and escaped over the Andes on horseback. His huge Canto General (1950) retells the history of the Americas from the side of its peoples.

He backed Salvador Allende and died twelve days after the 1973 coup that overthrew him. The official cause was cancer; whether he was poisoned is still unresolved.
sum: Chilean poet and diplomat, one of the most widely read poets of the 20th century. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1971.
